title: Week 11 Recap: Key Takeaways and Surprising Upsets from the 2026 NFL Sunday Games
body:
Sunday’s Week 11 slate delivered a mix of dominant performances, surprise upsets and storylines that will shape the playoff picture as the NFL heads toward the final stretch. The Buffalo Bills dismantled the Miami Dolphins in a 31‑10 blowout, while the Kansas City Chiefs secured a narrow 24‑21 win over the New York Jets in a Thursday night thriller that set up a Thanksgiving showdown with the Buffalo defense. Meanwhile, the San Francisco 49ers continued their resurgence with a gritty 28‑14 victory over the Detroit Lions, and the Dallas Cowboys finally snapped a three‑game losing streak with a 27‑13 triumph over the New England Patriots. The outcomes not only reinforced the Bills’ status as AFC East frontrunners but also highlighted vulnerabilities in teams that had been presumed secure in their divisions.

Buffalo’s performance against Miami was more than a simple win; it was a statement. The Bills’ defense forced three turnovers and limited the Dolphins to just 210 total yards, while quarterback Josh Allen threw for 285 yards and two touchdowns. The victory pushed Buffalo to a 9‑2 record, widening the gap with the New England Patriots and solidifying their claim as the AFC’s top seed. Defensive coordinator Leslie Frazier’s aggressive blitz packages kept Miami’s offense off balance, and the secondary’s three interceptions underscored a unit that has matured dramatically since last season. The win also gave head coach Sean McDermott a crucial week of rest before the Thursday night clash with Kansas City, a game many had labeled a “trap” that could expose the Bills’ secondary. Instead, the Bills entered the matchup with confidence, knowing they had already proven they can dominate a division rival.

Kansas City’s 24‑21 victory over the Jets was a tactical showcase by head coach Andy Reid, who relied heavily on Patrick Mahoney’s poise under pressure. Mahoney threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns, but also endured a sack and an interception that could have swung momentum in New York’s favor. The Chiefs’ defense, coordinated by Steve Spagnuolo, forced two turnovers and held the Jets to just 18 points, despite a late fourth‑quarter surge by the visitors. The win not only keeps Kansas City at 8‑3 but also sets up a high‑stakes Thanksgiving night clash with the Bills—an encounter that could determine the AFC East’s hierarchy and potentially alter the seeding for the postseason. The matchup will test whether the Chiefs can maintain their offensive rhythm while containing a Bills defense that has shown an ability to generate pressure without sacrificing coverage.

On the West Coast, the 49ers’ 28‑14 win over Detroit highlighted the resurgence of San Francisco’s defense and the continued development of quarterback Brock Purdy. Purdy’s efficient 245‑yard passing performance, coupled with a 65‑yard rushing touchdown, demonstrated his growing comfort in a system that now blends a stout defensive front with a versatile offense. Defensive end Nick Bosa recorded two sacks and a forced fumble, reinforcing the 49ers’ reputation as a defensive powerhouse. The victory moved San Francisco to 7‑4, keeping them within striking distance of the NFC West lead and underscoring their capacity to compete against both division rivals and non‑divisional opponents.

The Dallas Cowboys finally broke their three‑game slide with a convincing 27‑13 win over the Patriots, a result that revitalizes their playoff aspirations. Quarterback Dak Prescott delivered a balanced attack, passing for 210 yards and rushing for 68 yards, while the defense forced three turnovers and limited New England to a single field goal in the second half. The Cowboys’ resurgence can be traced to the mid‑season adjustments made by defensive coordinator Dan Quinn, whose emphasis on gap discipline has curbed the Patriots’ once‑potent run game. Dallas now sits at 6‑5, a record that still leaves them in the NFC East race but requires a strong finish to secure a postseason berth.

Looking ahead, the ramifications of Week 11 will echo through the remaining regular‑season games. Buffalo’s dominance over Miami and Kansas City’s narrow victory over the Jets set up a potential AFC East showdown that could determine the top seed. San Francisco’s steady climb suggests a possible NFC West power shift, while Dallas must sustain its momentum to avoid slipping back into mediocrity. As teams gear up for the crucial final stretch, the next few weeks will likely separate the true contenders from the pretenders, making the race to the playoffs more compelling than ever.
